podcast.title: Murder (1971)
podcast.body: King Curtis was tragically stabbed to death in the street outside his apartment building in 1971, at the age of 37. The incident occurred during an argument with two individuals who were conducting a drug deal near his door; he had asked them to move because he was trying to carry a heavy air conditioning unit into his building. "King Curtis was stopped to death in the street in 1971 outside his apartment building."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Collaborations (Year not specified)
podcast.body: King Curtis played saxophone on Buddy Holly's song "Reminiscing" as well as on Waylon Jennings's version of "Joli Blanc," contributing to experimental blends of genres. "King Curtain to play saxophone and reminiscing," and "This version had Holly on guitar and King Curtain's on saxophone, and is a really interesting attempt at blending Cajun music with R&B."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 74: "It Doesn't Matter Any More" by Buddy Holly

podcast.title: Integral to The Coasters' Sound
podcast.body: King Curtis's saxophone part on "Yakati Yak" became an integral element of The Coasters' musical formula, recurring in their subsequent records. His saxophone was considered more important to the overall sound of the records than the instrumental contributions of Adolf Jacobs. "King Curtis's saxophone part."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Saxophone Solo on "Bessermé Moucho"
podcast.body: King Curtis contributed a significant saxophone solo that comprised most of the second side of The Coasters' single for the old standard "Bessermé Moucho." "The second side mostly being a King Curtis saxophone solo."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
